prompt: Make the voiced B consonant, IPA b, as a single short burst. No 'buh', no vowel after it.

Make the CH sound, IPA tʃ: press the front of the tongue on the ridge behind the top teeth so the air is stopped for a moment, then release it with a short, sharp rush of air, like the start of 'chip'. One quick sound, about a quarter of a second. It must start with a stop, so it is not a plain SH. No vowel after it.
Make the voiced D sound, IPA d, as at the start of 'dog', a single short burst. No vowel after it.
Make a clean, voiceless F, IPA f, top teeth resting on the lower lip, held for one second. No vowel.
Make the voiced G consonant, IPA g, as in the start of 'go'. A single short burst. No 'guh'.
Make the H sound, IPA h, a single soft breath out, as at the start of 'hat'. No vowel after it.
Make the J sound, IPA dʒ, as at the start of 'jump': one short burst. No vowel after it, and do not say the letter name.
Make the voiceless K sound, IPA k, as at the start of 'cat', a single short burst. No vowel after it.

Make a held L, IPA l: press the tip of the tongue firmly on the ridge just behind the top front teeth and let your voice flow out over the sides of the tongue, like humming with the tongue up: 'llll'. Keep the tongue tip pressed the whole time. Hold it for one second. Not 'el', not 'oo', not any vowel.
Make the M sound, IPA m, lips closed, a steady hum held for one second. No vowel.

Make a held N, IPA n: lips apart, the tip of the tongue pressed on the ridge behind the top front teeth, and hum through the nose: 'nnnn'. Keep the lips open the whole time so it is not an M. Hold it for one second. No vowel.

Make a held NG, IPA ŋ, the sound at the end of 'sing': mouth open, tongue tip down, the back of the tongue pressed up against the soft palate, and hum through the nose: 'ngngng'. Keep the lips apart so it is not an M, and the tongue tip down so it is not an N. Hold it for one second. Do not say 'sing', no vowel.
Make only the voiceless P, IPA p, a single short puff of air. No vowel.
Make the English R consonant, IPA ɹ, as at the start of 'red'. Hold it for one second. Do not say 'ar' or 'rah'.
Make a clean, voiceless S, IPA s, like a snake hiss. Hold it for one second. No vowel.
Make a clean, voiceless SH, IPA ʃ, as in 'shoe', lips slightly rounded, held for one second. No vowel.
Make only a T sound, IPA t, a single short burst. No vowel.

Make the voiced TH, IPA ð: tongue tip resting lightly between the top and bottom front teeth, blow air out over it while using your voice, a soft buzz like the start of 'this' held out: 'dhhhh'. Hold it for one second. Not Z, not V, not D.

Make the voiceless TH, IPA θ: tongue tip resting lightly between the top and bottom front teeth, blow air out gently over it with no voice, a soft, flat hiss, quieter and less sharp than S, like the start of 'thin' held out: 'thhhh'. Hold it for one second. Not S, not F.
Make a voiced V, IPA v, top teeth resting on the lower lip with a buzz, held for one second. No vowel.

Make a W, IPA w: start with the lips tightly rounded and pushed forward, almost closed, then quickly open them. It is a fast movement, about a quarter of a second, not a held sound. Do not hold an 'oo' and do not add a vowel at the end.
Make only the Y sound, IPA j, as at the very start of 'yes': a quick glide about half a second long. Not a long 'ee', and no vowel after it.
Make only the voiced Z, IPA z, a buzzing hiss, held for one second. No vowel.
Make a labialized R, IPA ɹʷ: an English R made with strongly rounded lips, so it sounds partway between R and W. Hold it for one second. No vowel, and do not say a word.
Make a labialized retroflex R, IPA ɻʷ: tongue tip curled back and lips rounded, so it sounds like a rounded, slightly W-like R. Hold it for one second. No vowel, and do not say a word.
